title: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
gist: Netflix engineers describe replacing siloed, reactive monitoring with an AI-built operational ontology: Claude-driven harvesters turn Slack incident chaos into deterministic RDF triples in a graph database (QuipuDB) that feeds an AI SRE agent (AutoSRE), with a roadmap toward automatic root cause, auto-remediation and self-healing infrastructure.

insights.claim: Netflix peaked at 65 million concurrent streams during the Jake Paul vs Mike Tyson live boxing event at the end of 2024.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Shows live events stress-test streaming infra at unprecedented concurrency.

insights.claim: Netflix handles more than 2 billion app-to-server requests per day and upward of 38 million real-time logging events per second, across thousands of microservices and thousands of concurrent A/B tests.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Telemetry volume at this scale makes observability a data-engineering problem and a big cost center.

insights.claim: An 'average' recent Netflix incident took about four hours to resolve, paged nine teams, involved more than 30 engineers and triggered three related incidents; the root cause was a service that cut its capacity, causing backward-propagating errors.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Quantifies the human cost of incidents that AI SRE tooling aims to eliminate.
insights.quote: there are nine teams that were paged. More than 30 engineers were involved in the entire debugging process
insights.locator: Then, multiple teams are involved now

insights.claim: Netflix identifies four root causes of slow incident response: siloed MELT data stores, disconnected non-contextual alerting, complex triage, and downstream services 5-10 hops away never understanding user impact.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: A diagnostic framework for where AIOps vendors can create value.

insights.claim: Netflix's answer is 'connectedness': unify metrics, events, logs and traces into one MELT layer so dashboards, alerts, debugging and incident tools speak the same language.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Supports the investment case for unified observability platforms over point tools.
insights.locator: Given the vision that we saw

insights.claim: Traces are hard to use for debugging unless you already know which trace to look for, likened to finding a leaf in a dark forest blindfolded.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Questions the standalone value of distributed tracing products.

insights.claim: Connectedness is insufficient; Netflix needs explicit relationships between components, which it encodes as an 'observability ontology' using W3C standards RDF, OWL, SPARQL and SHACL.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Signals a revival of semantic-web tech as the grounding layer for AI agents in operations.

insights.claim: Netflix's harvest pipeline transforms every incident Slack message through deterministic enrichers (IDs from incident.io, PagerDuty, Jenkins regexes, catalog validation), observability APIs, then LLM classification, storing results in its graph database QuipuDB.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: A replicable blueprint for turning unstructured ops chatter into structured data.
insights.locator: With AI, we can do this much faster

insights.claim: The design goal is to create determinism from non-determinism: stochastic LLMs are constrained by a strong type system to emit deterministic, SPARQL-queryable triples.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Constraining LLMs with ontologies/typing is a pattern for reliable enterprise AI.
insights.quote: The paradox here is that we use stochastic tools to produce deterministic SPARQL queryable graph.
insights.locator: The goal is to create determinism

insights.claim: LLM classification is restricted to fixed taxonomies (e.g., a conversation is only an incident, question, discussion or decision) to prevent hallucinated categories.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Constrained output spaces are a practical guardrail for production LLM pipelines.

insights.claim: A 'knowledge flywheel' of observe, enrich, infer, adapt turns each incident's causal chain into a known pattern for the next incident.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Compounding incident knowledge creates a data moat for in-house or vendor AIOps.
insights.quote: The causal chain from one incident becomes a known pattern for the next.

insights.claim: Netflix runs Claude with the harvesting script in separate git worktrees per incident iteration; Claude both extracts data and fixes bugs in the harvesting script itself, producing many branches a human then asks Claude to cherry-pick and merge.

insights.so_what: Real production example of agents maintaining their own tooling with human-in-the-loop merges.

insights.claim: Netflix's AutoSRE AI SRE agent taps real-time MELT data, Slack, topology, devices, A/B test versions, the ontology and source code via MCPs and CLI tools, correlating far faster than humans.

insights.claim: Netflix's roadmap is automatic root cause analysis, then auto-remediation without human interaction (e.g., terminating instances for known patterns), then self-healing infrastructure that prevents alerts entirely.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan

insights.claim: The long-term vision is merging operational ontologies with data lineage into an enterprise ontology linking e.g. a pipeline data error by a specific team to bad clicks in the user service.
insights.speaker: Prasanna Vijayanathan
insights.so_what: Enterprise knowledge graphs could become a core AI infrastructure layer.

insights.claim: Quality control relies on a Swiss-cheese model of online-log metrics, frozen-input evals and human feedback, with plans for reinforcement learning from those signals.
